candidates.evidence_text: Families 'devastated' as Stretford school closure announced - BBC News Image caption, Sue Green says she does not want to move her five-year-old daughter Bethany from St Teresa's before it closes next year By Haider Saleem Reporting from Greater Manchester Published 1 hour ago Families say they are devastated by a decision to close a Catholic primary school in Greater Manchester. St Teresa's RC Primary School in Firwsood, Trafford, will close down in August 2027. One mother told the BBC she feared she might not be able to get a place for her daughter at another local Catholic school. The council said falling pupil numbers had made the school's finances unsustainable. Council figures show more than 50 pupils secured places at other primary schools before the decision, leaving just 39 on its roll. Helen Fitzpatrick, 39, whose daughter Delilah attends St Teresa's, said families were "absolutely devastated" by the decision, announced on Monday. Fitzpatrick, who helped organise a campaign against the closure, said she had contacted nearby St Ann's RC Primary School but was told it could not guarantee Delilah a place for September 2027. Although a place was available when she enquired, she said she would have had to accept it immediately. "Delilah isn't ready to leave St Teresa's until it closes," she said. She said she feared Delilah could "get lost in the crowd" at a larger school. Delilah said she was "very sad" about the school closing. Image caption, Helen fears she may struggle to secure a place at another nearby Catholic school for her eight-year-old daughter Delilah Another parent, Sue Green, said she faced a similar dilemma over her five-year-old daughter Bethany. Her three children have attended St Teresa's over the past 12 years. She said she had been told she would have to wait until July to apply for a September 2027 place, unless she transferred her daughter immediately. She said she did not want to disrupt Bethany's education by moving her before the school closed. "It's just so unfair," she said. Image caption, Sue Green, says she is worried about finding another Catholic primary school place when St Teresa's closes St Teresa's is a state-funded Catholic school whose budget is managed by its governing body. The Diocese of Salford owns the site and has a role in its Catholic governance, but Trafford Council oversees its finances, and made the decision to close it. Council documents show St Teresa's had 109 pupils in July. Of those, 21 left to attend secondary school, while 51 secured places at other primary schools for September. With two new reception pupils joining, the school had 39 children on its roll by the time of the council's October report. The council estimates that 24 pupils will need to move to another primary school when St Teresa's closes, while the remaining 15 will finish Year 6 and move to secondary school as normal. Parents and teachers believe the proposed closure encouraged families to move their children before councillors reached a final decision. The council acknowledged some families had moved early but said parents were entitled to seek places elsewhere at any time. It said it could not guarantee a child a place at a particular school, because admissions decisions depended on each school's arrangements. But it said three primary schools within a mile of St Teresa's had vacancies, along with two Catholic schools within 1.5 miles. Image caption, St Teresa's RC Primary School in Firswood, Stretford, is due to close in August 2027 after Trafford Council said falling pupil numbers had made its finances unsustainable Cameron Kennedy, 41, who has two daughters aged nine and five, said he felt more could have been done to save the school. "I don't really think it was given much of a chance," he said. Image caption, Cameron, whose two daughters attend St Teresa's, thinks more could have been done to save the school St Teresa's deficit stood at almost £196,000 at the end of 2025-26. It could exceed £1m by 2029-30 if the school remained open. A council spokesperson said: "We have had to make the difficult decision to close St Teresa's because of the significant fall in numbers of children over several years." The authority said it had worked with the school on its finances and explored alternatives, but was unable to identify a sustainable recovery plan. candidates.lead: The Grade II-listed Marble Arch has been serving pints on Manchester's Rochdale Road since 1888
candidates.evidence_text: Plans for 17-storey tower by historic Marble Arch pub rejected - BBC News Image source, LDRS Image caption, Plans for the 17-storey tower have prompted concerns over the Marble Arch's future By Declan Carey Local Democracy Reporting Service Published 1 hour ago Plans for a 17-storey tower block next to a historic Manchester pub have been rejected by councillors. Developer The McGoff Group had applied to build 153 flats beside the Grade II-listed Marble Arch on Rochdale Road, which has been serving customers since 1888. The company said the scheme would deliver much-needed city centre housing and help regenerate the area. But the pub's owners argued the development threatened its future, and Manchester City Council's planning committee voted to refuse the application. In its objection, the pub said the 17-storey building would be "overbearing and oppressive" and would harm the setting of the pub. Councillors also raised concerns about the impact of the development on the Marble Arch and the lack of affordable housing in the scheme. Councillor Jon-Connor Lyons said he was "deeply concerned" about the effect on "one of Manchester's distinctive and much-loved historic pubs". A member of staff told the Local Democracy Reporting Service : "We get tourists coming from all over the world who are sent here. "We have generations of families drinking here, dads and grandads and sons. You don't get places like this anymore and it's something we want to keep going." candidates.lead: Jawad Ali speaks out on the issue after capturing a racist outburst in footage shared widely online
candidates.evidence_text: Doorman who witnessed racist outburst says abuse becoming normal - BBC News Image caption, Jawad Ali, 20, said he now expects racial abuse when he goes to work By Kaya Black North West Published 22 October 2026 A doorman who shared a video of a racist outburst he witnessed while at work has said such abuse towards staff is becoming "normalised". The footage, taken outside Ko-Ko Lounge in Rochdale, Greater Manchester, showed a woman shouting abuse and making gestures at a black security guard. Jawad Ali said the club-goer became abusive after being asked to move away from an exit while he was working at the venue on Saturday night. Greater Manchester Police said it had received a report about the incident and inquiries were ongoing. To play this video you need to enable JavaScript in your browser. This video can not be played Figure caption, The video was shared widely on social media "It's disgusting," said Jawad, 20, who was working for Protective One Security at the time. He alleged the woman had also directed racial abuse towards him before the filming. Jawad said he decided to post the video on social media because "you can't do that and get away with it". "This isn't the first time, and it won't be the last," he added. Jawad said during the past two years working on the doors he has been called every racial slur and even threatened with death. "I expect now when I come to work to be racially abused one night out of the four that I work," he continued. "It's a normal thing now. It should be a big thing that gets prosecuted heavily." Image caption, The incident happened outside Ko-Ko Lounge in Rochdale Fellow security worker Liz Turley, who works for Radius Security, said: "There hasn't been a night where I haven't experienced some instance of somebody standing there for a prolonged period of time giving me abuse." She said staff were often subjected to racist, homophobic or sexist abuse on shift. "They will pick up on characteristics that we're likely to find offensive," she added. Jawad told the BBC he believed that online discourse about immigration issues had emboldened racist attitudes, particularly with narratives around "stopping the boats". "We haven't come off any boats. I was born here, my dad was born here, my granddad was born here," he said. "I've got just as much right to be here and work as anyone else does." Liz said she would like to see members of the public to stand up for others when they see these instances taking place. "Very often these individuals are left unchallenged in committing this sort of abuse," she said. candidates.lead: Gabrielle Debotte has told a jury Simon Richardson knew a cyclist was trapped under the wheels
candidates.evidence_text: The passenger in a car driven by her cousin which dragged a head teacher more than a mile to his death denied "not telling the truth" to "protect" herself Gabrielle Debotte, 27, had told a jury that driver Simon Richardson knew 56-year-old cyclist Michael Mullins was under the wheels of his car after colliding with him at a junction on 20 April Manchester Minshull Street Crown Court has heard Richardson drove on for 1.36 miles (2.2km) until father-of-two Mr Mullins was finally thrown free on a country lane in Lymm, Cheshire, where he died a short time later Richardson, 35, denies he knew Mr Mullins was under the wheels and has pleaded not guilty to murder and an alternative count of manslaughter A jury has heard Mr Mullins, who was cycling to his home in Northwich from Stretford Grammar School, died from injuries the prosecution claim were caused by "dragging and crushing" rather than the impact of the collision itself On Wednesday Debotte said a short time after Richardson accelerated away from the crash site, on Paddock Lane in Warburton, Trafford, they heard the sounds of "moaning" coming from under the vehicle

candidates.summary: Greater Manchester Police said 46 properties were damaged across Greater Manchester since 5 October

candidates.lead: Greater Manchester Police said 46 properties were damaged across Greater Manchester since 5 October
candidates.evidence_text: Social media a factor in HMO attacks, says police boss - BBC News Image source, LDRS/MEN Image caption, Police said there had been 46 properties damaged across the city region since 5 October By Naj Modak , North West and Ed Barnes , Local Democracy Reporting Service Published 22 October 2026 Social media is in part behind a spate of recent "racially or religiously motivated" attacks on houses in multiple occupation (HMOs) across Greater Manchester, a senior police officer has said. Greater Manchester Police said there had been 46 properties damaged across the city region since 5 October, including in Salford, Tameside and Stockport. Ch Sup Marcus Noden said footage of criminal damage was being shared widely "followed by comments and discussions", and people were using social media to "push the message out across different areas". He warned people to stop the attacks, which he said were "unlawful, reckless and putting lives at risk". As an investigation into the run of criminal damage continues, a 33-year-old man was arrested on Wednesday morning on suspicion of conspiracy to commit criminal damage and remained in custody for questioning. The damage was to HMOs or properties that were mistaken for HMOs. In Salford, 41 properties were targeted with three in Tameside and two in Stockport over the period. Image source, LDRS/MEN Image caption, Windows are seen boarded up on one property due to concerns of further attacks According to the Local Democracy Reporting Service , last week, two properties in Heaton Norris just outside Stockport town centre were targeted with anti-HMO graffiti. On Tuesday the window on one of the properties was smashed. Neither of the properties in Heaton Norris were currently used as HMOs, despite claims on social media. One is understood to be for sale while the owners of the property where the windows were smashed were asking Stockport Council for permission to convert it into an eight bedroom HMO. One of the owners, who wanted to remain anonymous, said he was planning to house young professionals if planning permission was approved. The vandalism and criminal damage follows similar incidents in Salford where suspected HMOs were targeted. Police said evidence suggests the attacked were linked to the criminal exploitation of children with a 13-year-old boy previously arrested. Image source, MEN Image caption, There are fears the violence has been fuelled by influencers on social media Noden said the force recognised that the spread of damage to properties across Greater Manchester would be worrying for residents. Speaking to BBC Radio Manchester , he said specially trained officers were looking into social media posts being circulated. To those on social media encouraging the attacked, Noden, said: "Stop what you are doing - lives are being put in danger". "I want to reiterate that we are taking this spate of damage extremely seriously and are continuing to relentlessly target offenders, including those who we believe are using and exploiting children to orchestrate the criminality," he said. Two men, aged 46 and 39 were also arrested on Monday for the same offence and released on bail. He said, "I hope it sends a strong message that anyone involved in this offending will be made to answer for their actions". Anyone with information that could support the investigation is being asked to contact the police. evidence_packet.evidence_text: Social media is in part behind a spate of recent "racially or religiously motivated" attacks on houses in multiple occupation (HMOs) across Greater Manchester, a senior police officer has said Greater Manchester Police said there had been 46 properties damaged across the city region since 5 October, including in Salford, Tameside and Stockport Ch Sup Marcus Noden said footage of criminal damage was being shared widely "followed by comments and discussions", and people were using social media to "push the message out across different areas" He warned people to stop the attacks, which he said were "unlawful, reckless and putting lives at risk" As an investigation into the run of criminal damage continues, a 33-year-old man was arrested on Wednesday morning on suspicion of conspiracy to commit criminal damage and remained in custody for questioning The damage was to HMOs or properties that were mistaken for HMOs

candidates.evidence_text: M62 crash causes eight-mile queues and one-hour delays - BBC News Image source, Highways England Image caption, National Highways reported delays of an hour and eight miles of congestion By Haider Saleem North West Published 22 October 2026 Drivers faced one-hour delays and eight-mile queues on the M62 following a crash during the morning rush hour. The collision happened on the eastbound carriageway between Junction 11 at Birchwood, near Warrington, and Junction 12 at the Eccles Interchange in Salford at about 06:35 BST. Greater Manchester Police said it appeared to involve several vehicles, but there had been no serious injuries or arrests - the road has since reopened. National Highways said one of the motorway's four lanes was closed for vehicle recovery at the time. Image source, Highways England Image caption, Long queues formed on the M62 eastbound following the early morning collision In an update at 08:38, the roads agency said drivers were facing delays of 60 minutes approaching the incident, with eight miles (13km) of congestion. Traffic camera images showed long queues of cars and lorries on the motorway. Police described the collision as involving vehicle damage only. candidates.evidence_text: Social workers received an anonymous tip-off that children were in "great danger" days before they were murdered in an arson attack, an inquest heard Demi Pearson, 14, her brother, Brandon, eight, and sisters, Lacie, seven, and Lia, three, died after petrol bombs were thrown into their home on Jackson Street, Walkden, Salford, in the early hours of December 11, 2017 Their mother Michelle Pearson, 37, died almost two years later after suffering severe burns A joint inquest into their deaths, now in its third week, is being heard at Bolton Coroners' Court and on Wednesday it heard of social services involvement with the family The hearing was told on 29 November, 2017, less than two weeks before the fatal attack, the social services department at Salford City Council received an anonymous call The caller said: "The children are in a really unsafe environment and in great danger."

candidates.evidence_text: Plans for a 17-storey tower block next to a historic Manchester pub have been rejected by councillors Developer The McGoff Group had applied to build 153 flats beside the Grade II-listed Marble Arch on Rochdale Road, which has been serving customers since 1888 The company said the scheme would deliver much-needed city centre housing and help regenerate the area But the pub's owners argued the development threatened its future, and Manchester City Council's planning committee voted to refuse the application In its objection, the pub said the 17-storey building would be "overbearing and oppressive" and would harm the setting of the pub Councillors also raised concerns about the impact of the development on the Marble Arch and the lack of affordable housing in the scheme

candidates.evidence_text: The family of an 86-year-old grandmother said her "agonising" wait in an emergency department rated by inspectors as one of the worst in England was an "absolute disgrace" Joan Jones was left "rolling over in pain" at the A&E department at Royal Albert Edward Infirmary in Wigan, Greater Manchester, her family said Her son, Barry Jones, said his mother had suffered a collapsed gallbladder and was in "constant pain" while waiting for treatment. He said it took 30 hours before she was admitted to a ward Wrightington, Wigan and Leigh Teaching Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust said it took the family's concerns "very seriously" and insisted cutting waiting times was a "key priority" Last month, a damning CQC inspection report found the hospital trust was one of the worst in the country for people spending more than 12 hours in the emergency department "The situation was unbelievable," said Barry Jones, 62, from Ashton-in-Makerfield

candidates.evidence_text: This year marks 100 years since Wythenshawe Hall was donated to Manchester Corporation At the time, the city was in urgent need of more housing In 1920 an urban planner called Patrick Abercrombie identified Wythenshawe as the only undeveloped land suitable for building a housing estate close to Manchester To turn his proposal into a reality, Ernest and Shena Simon bought Wythenshawe Hall from Robert Henry Grenville Tatton in 1926, which they donated to the city's corporation (now known as the council) The idea was that people could be rehoused away from industrial Manchester into what became known as the "Garden City" To celebrate 100 years, BBC North West Tonight has spoken to 100 people from the area about what Wythenshawe means to them

A senior officer said social media is partly behind the attacks, with footage shared widely and people using platforms to spread the message. candidates.evidence_text: Courts Driver was 'unaware' Stretford Grammar headteacher was trapped under car after hitting him, trial hears Simon Richardson, 35, denies murdering Michael Mullins Add to preferred sources News Amy Walker Court reporter 18:25, 22 Oct 2026 View 4 Ima A driver was 'not aware' that Stretford Grammar headteacher Michael Mullins was trapped under his car until he was finally dislodged, a murder trial has heard. Simon Richardson, 35, is accused of hitting popular educator Michael Mullins as he cycled home from work on April 20 Prosecutors allege Mr Richardson did not stop and 'put his foot down', dragging 56-year-old Mr Mullins along the road for 2.2km - 1.3 miles - before leaving him to die on a grass verge on Wet Gate Lane in Lymm Jurors previously heard witnesses described seeing Mr Richardson's Volvo ‘absolutely tanking it’ towards the junction of Dunham Road and Warburton Lane moments before the collision Mr Richardson denies murder; an alternate offence of manslaughter; and dangerous driving. Their mother Michelle, 37, died almost two years later from the injuries she suffered in the inferno, Bolton Coroners' Court has heard The attack on their home on Jackson Street, Walkden, Salford, on December 11, 2017 was carried out by Zak Bolland, 26, and an accomplice amid a ‘tit-for-tat’ feud with Ms Pearson’s eldest son Kyle, 16 On Thursday (October 22) the joint inquest heard evidence from Kate Kennedy, who was principal officer with Salford housing provider Salix Homes at the time She told how Ms Pearson attended the provider on November 27, 2017, and presented as ‘homeless’. She spoke with a case officer and a form produced following the visit, she said, stated the reason Ms Pearson wanted to be moved from her home of 14 years was to ‘flee from violence’

The Royton North councillor had led Oldham’s second largest party until he was replaced by Mark Wilkinson in September Mr Wilkinson then stood down as both leader of the group and Failsworth West councillor triggering a by-election. Add to preferred sources Comments News Declan Carey Local Democracy Reporter 06:08, 23 Oct 2026 View 2 Im There are fears that part of Manchester city centre could be ‘plunged into darkness’ if plans for seven new student accommodation blocks are built Councillors in the city were due to make a decision on two planning applications today (October 22) to build more than 3,500 student flats across seven new buildings, the tallest up to 50 storeys But elected officials agreed to postpone the decision amid concerns on daylight for existing city centre residents. They agreed to arrange site visits to the area ahead of deciding whether to approve or reject the proposals The homes were proposed in two planning applications aimed at boosting the number of student homes in the city. One scheme has been earmarked for the Charles Street multi-storey car park to build a total of 1,041 flats across three buildings The second is based on Sackville Street and would build a further 2,511 student homes in four buildings. candidates.evidence_text: Trafford 'They won't let me on the bus and it's all because of my dog' Ryan Hargreaves says he has been refused entry on multiple occasions because of his two-year-old French Bulldog Ed Add to preferred sources News Ramazani Mwamba News reporter 06:06 A dog owner says he has been repeatedly stopped from boarding Bee Network replacement buses because of his pet pooch - despite him being allowed on the services they are replacing Ryan Hargreaves says drivers have stopped him from boarding with his two-year-old French Bulldog at least five times. According to the 39-year-old, the issue usually arises when Atlantic Travel coaches are drafted in to support the network during travel disruptions in Trafford The Manchester Evening News understands it is Atlantic Travel's company policy to not allow animals onto their vehicles except for guide or hearing dogs. And Transport for Greater Manchester say it is down to the operator and driver's discretion whether dogs are allowed on board But Ryan, from Old Trafford, argues that his valid tram ticket should override the Atlantic Travel policy regarding animals "It's always with the same coach company," Ryan explained. "All the others are okay but it's this one specific company that seems to have their own rules."

candidates.evidence_text: Greater Manchester Police Two more cops latest of TEN to leave GMP in disgrace over contact with sex workers Sergeant Liam Smith and another cop, referred to only as 'Former Officer A', resigned from GMP ahead of separate disciplinary hearings View Im Add to preferred sources News John Scheerhout Crime reporter 06:05, 23 Oct 2026 Two more police officers have left GMP in disgrace following an internal force investigation which uncovered a band of cops contacting sex workers Sergeant Liam Smith and another cop, referred to only as 'Former Officer A' resigned from GMP ahead of separate disciplinary hearings which found them guilty of gross misconduct over contact with adult sex workers for no policing purpose They are the latest among the 10 GMP cops who have left GMP for contacting sex workers without a legitimate policing purpose. The force's Anti-Corruption Unit investigation was triggered by the case of Inspector Toby Knight. The disgraced cop scheduled hundreds of meetings with s Sergeant Smith made a series of contacts with sex workers while on and off duty. While off duty Sgt Smith used his work mobile to contact an adult sex worker on three occasions on August 3, 2024. He made two voice calls and and then sent a text, his disciplinary hearing was told The following month, on September 25, he again used his GMP device to call another number attributed to an adult sex worker while on duty just before midnight

Simon Richardson, 35, is accused of hitting popular educator Michael Mullins as he cycled home from work on April 20 Prosecutors allege Mr Richardson did not stop and 'put his foot down', dragging 56-year-old Mr Mullins along the road for 2.2km - 1.3 miles - before leaving him to die on a grass verge on Wet Gate Lane in Lymm Jurors previously heard witnesses described seeing Mr Richardson's Volvo ‘absolutely tanking it’ towards the junction of Dunham Road and Warburton Lane moments before the collision Mr Richardson denies murder; an alternate offence of manslaughter; and dangerous driving. He is on trial at Manchester's Minshull Street Crown Court On Thursday, jurors were told it was Mr Richardson’s case that he only realised Mr Mullins was underneath his car after he reversed his vehicle to return to the main road and his front seat passenger said there was “something” nearby

Simon Richardson, 35, is accused of hitting popular educator Michael Mullins as he cycled home from work on April 20 Prosecutors allege Mr Richardson did not stop and 'put his foot down', dragging 56-year-old Mr Mullins along the road for 2.2km - 1.3 miles - before leaving him to die on a grass verge on Wet Gate Lane in Lymm Jurors previously heard witnesses described seeing Mr Richardson's Volvo ‘absolutely tanking it’ towards the junction of Dunham Road and Warburton Lane moments before the collision Mr Richardson denies murder; an alternate offence of manslaughter; and dangerous driving. He is on trial at Manchester's Minshull Street Crown Court On Thursday, jurors were told it was Mr Richardson’s case that he only realised Mr Mullins was underneath his car after he reversed his vehicle to return to the main road and his front seat passenger said there was “something” nearby

candidates.evidence_text: Salford Michelle Pearson had requested house move two weeks before deadly firebombing, inquest told An inquest into the deaths of Michelle Pearson and four of her children is ongoing Add to preferred sources News Andrew Bardsley Court reporter 17:21, Housing bosses ruled against a request by the Pearson family for them to be rehomed two weeks before mum Michelle and four of her children were murdered in a petrol bomb attack on their home, an inquest has heard Demi, 15; Brandon, eight; Lacie, seven; and Lia, three, died after their house was firebombed. Their mother Michelle, 37, died almost two years later from the injuries she suffered in the inferno, Bolton Coroners' Court has heard The attack on their home on Jackson Street, Walkden, Salford, on December 11, 2017 was carried out by Zak Bolland, 26, and an accomplice amid a ‘tit-for-tat’ feud with Ms Pearson’s eldest son Kyle, 16 On Thursday (October 22) the joint inquest heard evidence from Kate Kennedy, who was principal officer with Salford housing provider Salix Homes at the time She told how Ms Pearson attended the provider on November 27, 2017, and presented as ‘homeless’. She spoke with a case officer and a form produced following the visit, she said, stated the reason Ms Pearson wanted to be moved from her home of 14 years was to ‘flee from violence’

Add to preferred sources Comments News Declan Carey Local Democracy Reporter 1 Rail travel around Greater Manchester is about to change forever with the first round of train stations set to join the Bee Network this December, with full integration across the region by 2030 The first 14 stations along the Glossop to Piccadilly line will join the network by the end of the year, with a further 15 from March 2027 including Stalybridge to Victoria and the Rose Hill, Marple and Hyde Loop lines Those stations will join Greater Manchester’s public transport network as part of the first phase of railway integration The second phase, by 2028, will see more key lines join the Bee Network with stations including Deansgate , Burnage, Stockport , Manchester Airport , Salford Central and Salford Crescent, Bolton , Rochdale , and Wigan Northwestern, among others The final phase of integration will be completed by 2030. The full roll out has been confirmed in a new Transport for Greater Manchester (TfGM) map published in a public report

candidates.evidence_text: Education 'Not the whole picture' blasts trust as two schools ranked worst for truancy in Greater Manchester Attendance and results have improved at both schools highlighted as England's worst for truancy Add to preferred sources Comments News Emma Gi An academy trust in charge of two schools ranked among England's worst for truancy says they are undergoing 'rapid transformation' and absence figures don't show the full picture We reported earlier this week how Department for Education figures showed that Buile Hill Academy in Salford and Denton Community Academy in Tameside were in the top 20 schools for worst unauthorised absence rates Buile Hill was sixth on the list, with an absence rate of 11%, while Denton Community was 16th with a rate of 10.3%. A third Greater Manchester school - Dixons Brooklands Dixons Brooklands Academy in Wythenshawe - was in joint 20th position with a rate of 9.9% Both Buile Hill and Denton Community are run by the Northern Education Trust (NET), which took control amid 'significant challenges' relating to attendance, behaviour and exam results View 6 Images Buile Hill Academy (Image: Kenny Brown | Manchester Evening News)

candidates.evidence_text: Oldham Former Oldham Reform leader resigns with immediate effect 'mid-investigation' Another councillor has also been suspended pending investigation in what is understood to be an unrelated case Add to preferred sources Comments News Edward Barnes Lo Former leader of Oldham Reform, councillor Lewis Quigg, has resigned mid-investigation while another elected member has been suspended, the party have said On October 22, Reform Oldham announced Coun Quigg had resigned from the party with immediate effect. The Royton North councillor had led Oldham’s second largest party until he was replaced by Mark Wilkinson in September Mr Wilkinson then stood down as both leader of the group and Failsworth West councillor triggering a by-election. Reform Oldham is now led by Waterhead Coun Paul Taylor The Manchester Evening News can also reveal St James Coun Gary Tarbuck has also been suspended from the party. The two cases are understood to not be linked When approached for comment, a Reform UK spokesman said: “Coun Tarbuck was suspended from Reform UK pending investigation. Coun Quigg resigned from the Reform group mid-investigation.”

Greater Manchester Police are concerned the evidence suggests a woman may have recently given birth Anyone with information, or who may have seen a woman in distress is asked to call police on 101 and quote incident number 684 of 22/10/2026 Detective Inspector Daniel Daly from GMP's Rochdale CID said: "Since receiving the report earlier today, we have been carrying out a number of lines of enquiry but our priority is to find the woman and make sure she is safe and well "She may be in need of urgent medical attention, and she is our absolute priority at the moment - that is why we are asking anyone with information to contact us." They agreed to arrange site visits to the area ahead of deciding whether to approve or reject the proposals The homes were proposed in two planning applications aimed at boosting the number of student homes in the city. candidates.evidence_text: Courts Driver was 'unaware' Stretford Grammar headteacher was trapped under car after hitting him, trial hears Simon Richardson, 35, denies murdering Michael Mullins Add to preferred sources News Amy Walker Court reporter 18:25, 22 Oct 2026 View 4 Ima A driver was 'not aware' that Stretford Grammar headteacher Michael Mullins was trapped under his car until he was finally dislodged, a murder trial has heard. Simon Richardson, 35, is accused of hitting popular educator Michael Mullins as he cycled home from work on April 20 Prosecutors allege Mr Richardson did not stop and 'put his foot down', dragging 56-year-old Mr Mullins along the road for 2.2km - 1.3 miles - before leaving him to die on a grass verge on Wet Gate Lane in Lymm Jurors previously heard witnesses described seeing Mr Richardson's Volvo ‘absolutely tanking it’ towards the junction of Dunham Road and Warburton Lane moments before the collision Mr Richardson denies murder; an alternate offence of manslaughter; and dangerous driving. He is on trial at Manchester's Minshull Street Crown Court On Thursday, jurors were told it was Mr Richardson’s case that he only realised Mr Mullins was underneath his car after he reversed his vehicle to return to the main road and his front seat passenger said there was “something” nearby

The money they earned was taken from them and mostly kept by the gang Marghiol took their passports off them, and they were unable to leave or ‘live a free life’, a court heard. He ‘controlled’ them through the fear of violence, using them as ‘punchbags’ during almost daily beatings in which he also sometimes used weapons such as a baseball bat and He also repeatedly sexually attacked them during what a judge described as ‘in effect a campaign of rape’

Add to preferred sources Comments News Declan Carey Local Democracy Reporter 1 Rail travel around Greater Manchester is about to change forever with the first round of train stations set to join the Bee Network this December, with full integration across the region by 2030 The first 14 stations along the Glossop to Piccadilly line will join the network by the end of the year, with a further 15 from March 2027 including Stalybridge to Victoria and the Rose Hill, Marple and Hyde Loop lines Those stations will join Greater Manchester’s public transport network as part of the first phase of railway integration The second phase, by 2028, will see more key lines join the Bee Network with stations including Deansgate , Burnage, Stockport , Manchester Airport , Salford Central and Salford Crescent, Bolton , Rochdale , and Wigan Northwestern, among others The final phase of integration will be completed by 2030. The full roll out has been confirmed in a new Transport for Greater Manchester (TfGM) map published in a public report

candidates.evidence_text: Salford Michelle Pearson had requested house move two weeks before deadly firebombing, inquest told An inquest into the deaths of Michelle Pearson and four of her children is ongoing Add to preferred sources News Andrew Bardsley Court reporter 17:21, Housing bosses ruled against a request by the Pearson family for them to be rehomed two weeks before mum Michelle and four of her children were murdered in a petrol bomb attack on their home, an inquest has heard Demi, 15; Brandon, eight; Lacie, seven; and Lia, three, died after their house was firebombed. Their mother Michelle, 37, died almost two years later from the injuries she suffered in the inferno, Bolton Coroners' Court has heard The attack on their home on Jackson Street, Walkden, Salford, on December 11, 2017 was carried out by Zak Bolland, 26, and an accomplice amid a ‘tit-for-tat’ feud with Ms Pearson’s eldest son Kyle, 16 On Thursday (October 22) the joint inquest heard evidence from Kate Kennedy, who was principal officer with Salford housing provider Salix Homes at the time She told how Ms Pearson attended the provider on November 27, 2017, and presented as ‘homeless’. She spoke with a case officer and a form produced following the visit, she said, stated the reason Ms Pearson wanted to be moved from her home of 14 years was to ‘flee from violence’

candidates.evidence_text: Education 'Not the whole picture' blasts trust as two schools ranked worst for truancy in Greater Manchester Attendance and results have improved at both schools highlighted as England's worst for truancy Add to preferred sources Comments News Emma Gi An academy trust in charge of two schools ranked among England's worst for truancy says they are undergoing 'rapid transformation' and absence figures don't show the full picture We reported earlier this week how Department for Education figures showed that Buile Hill Academy in Salford and Denton Community Academy in Tameside were in the top 20 schools for worst unauthorised absence rates Buile Hill was sixth on the list, with an absence rate of 11%, while Denton Community was 16th with a rate of 10.3%. A third Greater Manchester school - Dixons Brooklands Dixons Brooklands Academy in Wythenshawe - was in joint 20th position with a rate of 9.9% Both Buile Hill and Denton Community are run by the Northern Education Trust (NET), which took control amid 'significant challenges' relating to attendance, behaviour and exam results View 6 Images Buile Hill Academy (Image: Kenny Brown | Manchester Evening News)

candidates.evidence_text: Oldham Former Oldham Reform leader resigns with immediate effect 'mid-investigation' Another councillor has also been suspended pending investigation in what is understood to be an unrelated case Add to preferred sources Comments News Edward Barnes Lo Former leader of Oldham Reform, councillor Lewis Quigg, has resigned mid-investigation while another elected member has been suspended, the party have said On October 22, Reform Oldham announced Coun Quigg had resigned from the party with immediate effect. The Royton North councillor had led Oldham’s second largest party until he was replaced by Mark Wilkinson in September Mr Wilkinson then stood down as both leader of the group and Failsworth West councillor triggering a by-election. Reform Oldham is now led by Waterhead Coun Paul Taylor The Manchester Evening News can also reveal St James Coun Gary Tarbuck has also been suspended from the party. The two cases are understood to not be linked When approached for comment, a Reform UK spokesman said: “Coun Tarbuck was suspended from Reform UK pending investigation. Coun Quigg resigned from the Reform group mid-investigation.”

Greater Manchester Police are concerned the evidence suggests a woman may have recently given birth Anyone with information, or who may have seen a woman in distress is asked to call police on 101 and quote incident number 684 of 22/10/2026 Detective Inspector Daniel Daly from GMP's Rochdale CID said: "Since receiving the report earlier today, we have been carrying out a number of lines of enquiry but our priority is to find the woman and make sure she is safe and well "She may be in need of urgent medical attention, and she is our absolute priority at the moment - that is why we are asking anyone with information to contact us." Shortly after 4.30pm, police confirmed that mother and baby had been found. They said: "Thank you to all who helped with our appeal for information after evidence was found to suggest that a woman had recently given birth near to the junction of Watkins Street and Charter Street

candidates.evidence_text: Crime Gang used cruel cash machine trick to steal thousands from pensioners The three men would work together to distract their 'vulnerable' targets Add to preferred sources News Ashlie Blakey Live and breaking news reporter 13:49, 22 Oct 2026 View 4 Three members of an organised crime gang have been jailed after they stole thousands of pounds from pensioners across the country using a cruel trick at cash machines Ionut Matei, 40, Vasile Ciubotaru, 45, and Ramonel Mandache, 51, together stole more than £40,000 from their 'vulnerable' victims. The trio targeted people using ATMs in Halifax bank, including in the Stockport and Bury branches, and at Lloyds Bank Detectives found Matei, Ciubotaru and Mandache, who are all Romanian nationals, would travel across the country during their malicious enterprise. To trick their victims, one of the men would stand close enough to see them entering their pin into the cash machine Another would distract them by drawing attention to a banknote deliberately placed on the floor nearby, Cheshire Police said. The third man would then swipe their bank card and replace it with a similar-looking card Victims were left completely unaware that their card had been stolen. The gang would then use the stolen cards and PIN to withdraw cash and buy items, often before the victims had realised what had happened

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Crime Gang used cruel cash machine trick to steal thousands from pensioners The three men would work together to distract their 'vulnerable' targets Add to preferred sources News Ashlie Blakey Live and breaking news reporter 13:49, 22 Oct 2026 View 4 Three members of an organised crime gang have been jailed after they stole thousands of pounds from pensioners across the country using a cruel trick at cash machines Ionut Matei, 40, Vasile Ciubotaru, 45, and Ramonel Mandache, 51, together stole more than £40,000 from their 'vulnerable' victims. The trio targeted people using ATMs in Halifax bank, including in the Stockport and Bury branches, and at Lloyds Bank Detectives found Matei, Ciubotaru and Mandache, who are all Romanian nationals, would travel across the country during their malicious enterprise. To trick their victims, one of the men would stand close enough to see them entering their pin into the cash machine Another would distract them by drawing attention to a banknote deliberately placed on the floor nearby, Cheshire Police said. The third man would then swipe their bank card and replace it with a similar-looking card Victims were left completely unaware that their card had been stolen. The gang would then use the stolen cards and PIN to withdraw cash and buy items, often before the victims had realised what had happened

candidates.evidence_text: Salford Inside the glamorous Art Deco Salford home given listed status Broughton Park property is 91 years old Add to preferred sources Comments News Neal Keeling Chief reporter 06:18, 22 Oct 2026 Updated 11:51, 22 Oct 2026 View 5 Images The 1935 hous A family home in Salford has been given Grade II listed status. The property on Old Hall Lane, Broughton Park, is described by experts as a "strikingly glamorous" house Built in 1935 it is a rare example of the international Streamline Moderne style that evolved from Art Deco. It features curved corners, long horizontal "speed lines," and a sleek, machine-age look inspired by ocean liners, airplanes, and trains Other examples of the style include East Finchley Tube Station in London and the Coca Cola building in Los Angeles. The design is characterised by flat roofs, horizontal emphasis, curved corners and dramatic glazing From the outside, this house is distinguished by slim brown brick facades, a flat roof, an exposed white concrete base, and windows that span both curved and angled corners View 5 Images A curved stair tower dominates the back of the house, while the entrance front steps back in stages, with an original single-storey garage reflecting the growing importance of the car in home design between the First and Second World Wars

The holidaymakers, who paid up to £3,000 each, claim they encountered an 'overp They said they raised concerns about hygiene in buffet restaurants where flies could be seen around uncovered food. Many were left confined to their cabins during the eight-night trip, while others were hospitalised when they returned back to the UK The group have now instructed international injury lawyers to investigate their illnesses. P&O said they are 'aware' of groups correspondence and 'take such reports seriously' Julie Stones, 53, from Bolton, was among those who fell ill. She said the illness left her battling a catalogue of health problems

candidates.evidence_text: Monday 12 October 2026 at 5:22pm Credit: Family photo A police officer called to the home of a mother and her four children murdered hours later in an arson attack told a court she thought their killer was making "empty threats" and did not try to arrest him Pc Gemma Quinn told Bolton Coroner's Court she did not think it necessary to arrest Zak Bolland, 26, "there and then" after a 999 call from Michelle Pearson , 37, when he threatened her son and home on Jackson Street in Walkden , Salford Greater Manchester Police's (GMP) Pc Quinn said she planned to arrest Bolland when she was next on shift in two days' time But after she and a more junior colleague left Ms Pearson's home, Bolland returned less than three hours later to murder her and four of her children in a firebomb attack in the early hours of December 11 2017 The firebombing killed four of Michelle's children, Demi Pearson, 15, her brother Brandon, eight, and sisters Lacie, seven, and Lia, three Zak Bolland, 26, and David Worrall, 28, were both jailed for life the following year for the murders

Credit: via planning documents FCHO replaces contractor for £3.7m affordable Royton flats 22 October 2026 09:47 Julia Hatmaker Comments ( ) Robwood Construction was meant to complete the 30-apartment project in 2024. Now, two years later, John Southworth Builders has been brought on to salvage the Oldham scheme and see it delivered by the end of July 2027. First Choice Homes Oldham appointed Robwood in May 2022 to build 15 one-bed and 15 two-bed flats on the former High Barn Resource Centre site in Royton. The £3.7m scheme, which was led by Lancet Homes and designed by MPSL, is due to be completely affordable rent and achieve an EPC rating of B. Now, Robwood has been wound up after undergoing compulsory liquidation. FCHO terminated its contract with Robwood in June due to “unacceptable delays.” Inspections by new contractor John Southworth have found defects in the existing construction work that will require correction, FCHO said. The group noted that John Southworth will start on site within a few weeks, with an aim towards finishing the scheme in July 2027. FCHO deputy chief executive Andy Ewart stressed that the project would be completed. “We share the frustration about the length of time this development has taken but we now have a contractor, a detailed plan and visible progress will soon be seen on site.” To review the original plans for the site, search reference FUL/347787/21 on Oldham Council’s planning portal. She’s wearing Musera, which looks to be Manchester’s friendliest, chicest new clothing label — launched in 2024 from an From this Newton Street office, a band of young designers turn out a stream of trend pieces: low-rise trousers and asymmetric tops, distressed knitwear and leopard-print flares, western fringed jumpers and A-level prom gowns. Their Instagram bio lauds the brand as “Est. MCR.” Over a million people watched the staff dancing around their Northern Quarter office to Whigfield’s Saturday Night on TikTok. More still tuned in to a video showing them kitted out in Musera for Drake’s performance at Co-op Live last year. And who knows how many have sidestepped “Be a muse in your own era,” goes their slogan; presumably also the source of their similarly recondite name. Their Instagram captions are a list of internet cliches verging on parody. “My blood type is iced latte,” reads one post Looking at this well-curated online presence, you might well be convinced that Musera is, as they suggest, Manchester through and through

Many junior staff members believe raising issues will lead to retaliation, and 59% of survey respondents have witnessed or experienced a form of harassment, discrimi One worker recalled a young apprentice being repeatedly sexually harassed by a senior colleague until she was forced to leave the council. “He was allowed to stay,” they said of the offending staffer. “She was interviewed by two male managers and needless to say she left.” There A council worker, speaking to us on the condition of anonymity, said of the report: “if I were a manager that would sicken me to my core.” When we approached the council before publishing this story, CEO Tom Stannard said: “it is completely unacceptable that anyone should feel undervalued, unable to raise concerns, unsupported if they do or – in the worst cases – unsafe. These issues cannot and will not be ignored.”

Since announcing free subscriptions for 16-25 year olds yesterday, almost half of them have already been snapped up! Click the button to sign up, and don't faf Ella took the final drag of her cigarette outside the Rat and Pigeon pub, dropped it down on the ground, stamped on it, and bent over to pick it up. She usually stubbed her finished cigs against her trainers, before placing them in a bin, but she had heels on and didn’t want to r A man, dressed in all black, wearing a jacket with Manchester City Council sewn on it and a camera mounted on his chest, appeared from behind the dustbins on Back Piccadilly, a grubby alley in the Northern Quarter. He said he was going to fine her for dropping litter. evidence_packet.evidence_text: A public consultation has opened on changes that could affect who secures one of the sought-after grammar school's 204 Year 7 places Share on WhatsApp Share via Email Girls living close to Altrincham Grammar School for Girls could lose priority for places to children attending four designated primary schools under proposed changes to its admissions policy A public consultation has opened on plans to give pupils from four primary schools belonging to the same academy trust as AGGS priority over other applicants who have passed the entrance examination – even if they live closer to the school The proposals, which would take effect from September 2028, could have significant implications for Altrincham families whose daughters attend local primary schools outside Bright Futures Educational Trust Under the existing admissions system, girls who pass the entrance examination and live within the school's eight-mile catchment area are generally prioritised according to how close they live to AGGS, after higher-priority categories have been considered But the proposed arrangements would introduce a new category giving preference to qualifying pupils attending four primary schools within Bright Futures Educational Trust

The women waived their right to anonymity to tell their harrowing stories as part of a BBC investigation that uncovered more than 1,200 domestic abuse allegations made in three years against police officers and special constables across England and Wales Professional standards investigations were opened into allegations including rape, sexual assault, grievous bodily harm, stalking and serious violence Most cases were discontinued, subjected to no further action or dropped because of a lack of evidence or victims withdrawing their complaints Campaigners say more needs to be done to tackle police-perpetrated abuse despite repeated warnings about failures to identify and remove dangerous officers in the wake of the 2021 murder of Sarah Everard in London by serving Metropolitan Police officer Wayne Couzens

candidates.evidence_text: Gabrielle Debotte, 27, had told a jury that driver Simon Richardson knew 56-year-old cyclist Michael Mullins was under the wheels of his car after colliding with him at a junction on 20 April Manchester Minshull Street Crown Court has heard Richardson drove on for 1.36 miles (2.2km) until father-of-two Mr Mullins was finally thrown free on a country lane in Lymm, Cheshire, where he died a short time later Richardson, 35, denies he knew Mr Mullins was under the wheels and has pleaded not guilty to murder and an alternative count of manslaughter A jury has heard Mr Mullins, who was cycling to his home in Northwich from Stretford Grammar School, died from injuries the prosecution claim were caused by "dragging and crushing" rather than the impact of the collision itself On Wednesday Debotte said a short time after Richardson accelerated away from the crash site, on Paddock Lane in Warburton, Trafford, they heard the sounds of "moaning" coming from under the vehicle She told the jury her "panicking" cousin then wound his window down and said "he's under the car"

candidates.evidence_text: Tributes are being paid to Councillor Pat Karney, who has died aged 78 after serving the city for almost half a century Cllr Karney, who was receiving treatment for cancer and grateful for the excellent care he received at The Christie, has represented Harpurhey as a councillor since 1979 and has been one of the city’s most prominent politicians for much of that time Closest to his heart was always Collyhurst/Harpurhey and north Manchester and enthusiastically advocating investment in, and celebration of, the area For many years Pat has been known as a champion and spokesperson for the city’s popular Christmas Markets and festive events, as well as acting as city centre spokesperson He was one of the pivotal figures in the regeneration of the city centre after it was devastated by the 1996 IRA bomb, Chairing the City Centre Committee established to oversee the rebirth. He has been a director of Cityco, the not-for-profit city centre management company, since Manchester Day, the annual celebration of the city first held in 2010, was his brainchild and will be among his legacies

candidates.evidence_text: Experience Bolton’s FREE winter light art festival and enjoy four unforgettable nights of spectacular illuminated installations, captivating performances, and immersive experiences for all ages Curated in partnership by Bolton Council and Things That Go On Things, Put Big Light On Festival will run from Thursday 19 November to Sunday 22 November across Bolton town centre, between 5pm and 9pm every day With illuminated installations, roaming performers, and larger-than-life creations, the festival will showcase a mix of contemporary outdoor arts and family-friendly performances designed to surprise and delight audiences At the heart of this year’s festival, the Loom of Light by dbnAudile will take inspiration from Bolton’s textile heritage to transform Victoria Square into a mesmerising and striking walk-through artwork Using illuminated threads of light and colour to create an evolving structure that visitors can explore from within, this showstopping and interactive feature offers a contemporary interpretation of the weaving traditions that helped shape the town’s textile history Stretching across the square, the installation promises a memorable visual experience, with glowing strands of light creating a dramatic backdrop for photographs, exploration, and discovery throughout the festival

candidates.evidence_text: Wigan Council is introducing new orders to tackle anti-social behaviour in Wigan and Leigh town centres, including targeted powers against e-bikes and scooters These Public Space Protection Orders (PSPOs) will be in place for three years to support the police, council and other authorities in tackling a wide range of issues, reduce crime and help people feel safer in their communities This introduction follows an extensive review of previous orders and a public consultation held over the summer which gathered significant feedback from residents, businesses and the community sector Councillor Kevin Anderson, cabinet portfolio holder for Police, Crime and Civil Contingencies, said: “Residents, businesses and visitors all took part in our consultation, and it was clear that anti-social behaviour remains a concern “Most people who visit, live and work in our town centres do so responsibly, and these orders are aimed at addressing the small number of behaviours that negatively impact our communities, while ensuring support remains available for those who may be vulnerable.” The orders prohibit several anti-social behaviours, with new powers to enforce against anti-social use of cycles, e-bikes and scooters, and drug-related litter and paraphernalia

candidates.evidence_text: Experience the raw, unfiltered power of Balkan folklore in a new immersive show from the world’s most famous performance artist Balkan Erotic Epic is a bold new performance work created by the iconic artist Marina Abramović . Regarded as the world’s most influential performance artist, Abramović’s transformative work has reached millions of people – from opening the Pyramid Stage at Glastonbury Festival t A four-hour ritual where ancient myth meets performance art, Balkan Erotic Epic explores the eroticism, spirituality and traditions of Abramović’s homeland through 13 visceral scenes Brought to life by a cast of over 70 performers, dancers, musicians and singers, the experience unfolds across Aviva Studios. Audiences are free to choose their own path – with pop-up encounters punctuating the action, bringing bodies together in dance, song and ritual Watch Fertility Rite , a fevered ritual where bodies writhe against the ground in a desperate call for fertility. History, power and empire collide in Button Up! – a major new exhibition from the world-leading artist and activist Ai Weiwei . Internationally renowned artist and activist Ai Weiwei turns his critical gaze to the last 200 years of global history with this major new exhibition. Monumental in scale and ambition, Ai Weiwei: Button Up! is the artist’s most expansive presentation in the North to date.. Ai Weiwei is known around the world for his uncompromising artistic vision and political activism. From a childhood in exile to surviving secret detention in China, his remarkable life and career have led him to global prominence. Using sculpture, installation, film, photography and architecture, his work is unafraid to ask urgent, critical questions.. In Button Up! , the artist turns his lens on two centuries of Chinese and British relations. Taking inspiration from Manchester, a city at the heart of the Industrial Revolution, Button Up! explores how historic systems of trade, empire and exploitation resonate in today’s humanitarian and political crises.. Conceived as a total environment, Ai Weiwei: Button Up! brings together new and existing large-scale works on display in the UK for the first time. The monumental installation features porcelain, cotton, glass, bronze and even buttons and toy bricks. Each material contains a story of human invention and consumption. Together, they paint a picture of globalisation.. Both global and personal, the title Button Up! is a playful poke at the artist’s ongoing battle with censorship. The exhibition also features the world premiere of a new body of work created especially for the vast spaces of the Warehouse – Eight-Nation Alliance Flags made from millions of buttons, as well as a new version of History Of Bombs made entirely from toy bricks.. The new commissions sit alongside large-scale works by the artist which are going on show in the UK for the first time: Law of the Journey (2017), a 47m long inflatable migrant boat containing hundreds of human figures and the artist’s largest artwork to date; Wang Family Ancestral Hall (2015), a Ming dynasty ancestral temple reassembled from 1,500 individual wooden pieces ; and La Commedia Umana (2017-21), a black Murano glass chandelier made up of over 2,000 pieces and weighing nearly 3 tonnes. Also on show is Circle of Animals/Zodiac Heads (2010), a re-envisioning of the twelve animals of the Chinese zodiac.. Button Up! immerses visitors in Ai Weiwei’s fearless interrogation of the forces past and present that drive today’s injustices – while championing art’s enduring power to challenge and inspire.. . . . “I’m not interested in making very big things just for the sake of it. But in Manchester, that wonderful Warehouse space calls for monumental work. Visiting the city for this exhibition – the birthplace of the Industrial Revolution – and reflecting on Britain’s global territorial expansion made me realise I had to explore that history and understand how it connects to the forces driving today’s wars and global crises. The world today is deeply divided, with tragedy all around. Understanding history goes hand in hand with standing up for truth and justice.”. Ai Weiwei. . . Explore. . Ai Weiwei | Dream Space . evidence_packet.evidence_text: History, power and empire collide in Button Up! – a major new exhibition from the world-leading artist and activist Ai Weiwei History, power and empire collide in Button Up! – a major new exhibition from the world-leading artist and activist Ai Weiwei Internationally renowned artist and activist Ai Weiwei turns his critical gaze to the last 200 years of global history with this major new exhibition. Monumental in scale and ambition, Ai Weiwei: Button Up! is the artist’s most expansive presentation in the North to date Ai Weiwei is known around the world for his uncompromising artistic vision and political activism. From a childhood in exile to surviving secret detention in China, his remarkable life and career have led him to global prominence. Using sculpture, installation, film, photography In Button Up! , the artist turns his lens on two centuries of Chinese and British relations. Taking inspiration from Manchester, a city at the heart of the Industrial Revolution, Button Up! explores how historic systems of trade, empire and exploitation resonate in today’s humani Conceived as a total environment, Ai Weiwei: Button Up! brings together new and existing large-scale works on display in the UK for the first time. The monumental installation features porcelain, cotton, glass, bronze and even buttons and toy bricks. Each material contains a stor Both global and personal, the title Button Up! is a playful poke at the artist’s ongoing battle with censorship. It can feel busy and overwhelming without much clarity on what’s actually working. This programme is about helping people step back, put the right foundations in plac The Monthly Marketing Programme is delivered through a structured monthly format, with immediate access to a starter guide on sign-up. It’s available from £49 per month, with no long-term commitment

candidates.evidence_text: Finish work and unwind with live music from Manchester’s best jazz musicians. Beat the Jams live series showcases the very best of the jazz scene, at short rush hour gigs from 6pm at Band on the Wall. What better way to avoid those endless queues, chaotic traffic and stressful homeward journeys? Clock off and skip the rush-hour traffic while you watch live jazz and make the most of our happy hour deals from 5–7pm: £4.50 pints / 2 for £15 cocktails / £15 bottles of wine + pizzas from £5! The new season kicks off on 24 September with tenor saxophonist Dean Masser and pianist Richard Wetherall, followed by: 7 October – Anna Chandler-King Quartet Leeds based saxophonist and composer Anna joins us again for Beat the Jams, this time with her own band. Anna’s thoughtful and inventive compositions are firm favourites of us at Beat the Jams and her quartet promises to be a unique rush hour busting treat! 16 November – Sam Lightwing Quartet Saxophonist and composer Sam Lightwing brings presents brand new music for his thrilling young quartet, showcasing Sam’s original compositions, which blend classic mainstream jazz grooves with modern flavours of post-pop and latin, all wrapped up in the language of contemporary sax giants such as Chris Potter, Seamus Blake and Joshua Redman. 15 December – Svarc/Devine/Walsh with Richard Iles The band combines deep pocket, fearless interplay and a shared love of exploration. Expect everything from soulful melodies and infectious rhythms to moments of exhilarating collective improvisation, delivered with the chemistry that only world-class musicians can create. Tickets from £13 per show, or £42 for a season ticket

evidence_packet.summary: Finish work and unwind with live music from Manchester’s best jazz musicians. Beat the Jams live […] The post Beat the Jams Autumn season announced appeared first on Band on the Wall
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Finish work and unwind with live music from Manchester’s best jazz musicians. Beat the Jams live series showcases the very best of the jazz scene, at short rush hour gigs from 6pm at Band on the Wall. What better way to avoid those endless queues, chaotic traffic and stressful homeward journeys? Clock off and skip the rush-hour traffic while you watch live jazz and make the most of our happy hour deals from 5–7pm: £4.50 pints / 2 for £15 cocktails / £15 bottles of wine + pizzas from £5! The new season kicks off on 24 September with tenor saxophonist Dean Masser and pianist Richard Wetherall, followed by: 7 October – Anna Chandler-King Quartet Leeds based saxophonist and composer Anna joins us again for Beat the Jams, this time with her own band. Anna’s thoughtful and inventive compositions are firm favourites of us at Beat the Jams and her quartet promises to be a unique rush hour busting treat! 16 November – Sam Lightwing Quartet Saxophonist and composer Sam Lightwing brings presents brand new music for his thrilling young quartet, showcasing Sam’s original compositions, which blend classic mainstream jazz grooves with modern flavours of post-pop and latin, all wrapped up in the language of contemporary sax giants such as Chris Potter, Seamus Blake and Joshua Redman. 15 December – Svarc/Devine/Walsh with Richard Iles The band combines deep pocket, fearless interplay and a shared love of exploration. Expect everything from soulful melodies and infectious rhythms to moments of exhilarating collective improvisation, delivered with the chemistry that only world-class musicians can create. Tickets from £13 per show, or £42 for a season ticket

From ancient airs to future soundscapes, The Olllam is not just carrying the tradition forward—they’re reinventing it

candidates.evidence_text: This year's nominations for Manchester's best bar, best restaurant and best chef are now open Go to Manchester's Finest X profile The Manchester Food and Drink Festival (MFDF) Awards have revealed their 2026 shortlists, with some of Greater Manchester’s best-known restaurants, bars, pubs, cafés and independent food businesses among the nominees The awards ceremony will take place on Monday 25 January 2027, moving to City Hall at Medlock Square for the first time. The new entertainment district is home to a growing collection of bars and restaurants, including Zadie’s and Little Beast Sponsored by Therme Manchester, the awards will recognise businesses and individuals across 17 categories, covering everything from affordable eats and neighbourhood venues to independent producers and the region’s leading chefs Among those competing for Restaurant of the Year are Kallos, Stow, Higher Ground, Winsome, Erst, The Pearl, Adam Reid at The French and The Trof The Chef of the Year shortlist includes Jamie Pickles of Stow, Shaun Moffatt of Winsome, Jess Furniss of WTLGI, Gary Weir of Open Fire and Tartuffe, Sian Wilson of Bar Posie, Tom Barnes of Skof, Rosie Maguire of Higher Ground and Brit Wardle of 10 Tib Lane

candidates.evidence_text: The LGBTQ+ bar returns on Tariff Street with cocktails, food, live jazz, drag and late-night DJ sets By Manchester's Finest, Last updated 14 October 2026 Go to Manchester's Finest X profile LGBTQ+ cocktail bar Red Light will reopen in Manchester’s Northern Quarter on Friday 9 October, taking over a new space on Tariff Street The bar, founded by Deana Ferguson, will return next door to The Whisky Jar with a new look, an expanded food and drink menu and a programme of live music, DJs and performance The new Red Light features booth seating, a bar and club-style space, red lighting and an outdoor terrace, which will remain open until 11pm. Its interiors will also showcase work from queer local photographers Jen Melia, Sara Carpentieri, Nick Priestley and Harmeet Singh A number of cocktails from Red Light’s original menu will return, including the Pink Picante and Pomme Verte, its take on an appletini. Other returning drinks include the Belfast Coffee, spicy pickle martini Especiado and Pornstar Chic, made with homemade passionfruit sorbet

candidates.evidence_text: It’s been a busy week at Labour Party Conference in Liverpool, with technology, growth and devolution featuring heavily in many of the conversations we’ve been part of In his first Conference speech as Prime Minister, Andy Burnham talked about devolving more power to places, backing businesses to grow and taking some of what has worked in Greater Manchester into a wider national approach. He also confirmed that AI will be a central focus of the That felt particularly relevant following an event we hosted through the UK Tech Cluster Group with AI Minister Kanishka Narayan, North East Mayor Kim McGuinness and other regional leaders, looking at AI, devolution and local growth One of the clearest themes from the discussion was that devolution should not mean every place trying to build the same thing. Different regions have different strengths, assets and specialisms, and there was a strong view that greater collaboration between places could create bi Procurement and buying local also featured strongly. The discussion highlighted the role public sector buying power can play in supporting regional businesses, helping successful pilots move into commercial contracts and strengthening UK capability in areas such as AI and cyber There was also a broader conversation about sovereignty and the UK’s role internationally. The discussion was not about trying to own every part of the AI stack, but about understanding where the UK already has genuine capability and where it makes sense to build more. Strengths

candidates.summary: A star of BusinessCloud’s Founder 250 list will discuss the rapid success of his HR tech startup at FUEL Manchester next week. candidates.lead: A star of BusinessCloud’s Founder 250 list will discuss the rapid success of his HR tech startup at FUEL Manchester next week.
candidates.evidence_text: Founder 250 star to bring ‘grit, innovation, authenticity’ to FUEL Manchester Posted on October 23, 2026 by Jonathan Symcox Founder 250 star to bring ‘grit, innovation, authenticity’ to FUEL Manchester Tom Keighley to discuss rapid growth of HR tech startup urfuture, recently named fifth most downloaded business app ahead of Zoom Share: Listen to article Founders A star of BusinessCloud’s Founder 250 list will discuss the rapid success of his HR tech startup at FUEL Manchester next week. CEO Tom Keighley (pictured right) co-founded urfuture in Preston in 2024 with COO Jayel Williams (left) and CCO Holly Hobbs (centre). It moved to Manchester at the start of the year before raising £1.7 million in seed investment . The firm is looking to replace CVs and job boards with tech solutions for the AI era. In August, urfuture became the fifth most downloaded business app, ahead of Zoom and just behind Indeed, Teams, LinkedIn and WhatsApp. Keighley, whose work in the talent space dates back to 2011, said the moment meant he “literally had to pause to take it in”. “These are some of the biggest brands in the world with enormous teams, budgets, reach and resources but we have something money can’t buy,” he wrote on LinkedIn. “Grit. Innovation. Authenticity and three incredible individuals who don’t just understand the audience we’re trying to reach, they are that audience.” On Wednesday 28th October, he will speak on the breakfast panel at FUEL Manchester. You can sign up for free at the link below . Register for breakfast panel & networking River Capital led the £1.7m investment, with participation from SyndicateRoom’s Access fund, Manchester Angels, Fhunded, Solid Bond, Host Capital and a number of sector specialist angels. The investment comes as the number of young people aged 16 to 24 not in education, employment or training approaches one million. The problem is being compounded as 45% of job seekers now use AI to help write or edit their CVs, meaning employers are increasingly overwhelmed with high volumes of low-quality, irrelevant applications. The startup is building a new hiring platform that combines a social-first Gen Z distribution engine with a proprietary behavioural science job matching algorithm. This enables employers to identify higher-intent, more diverse candidates and reduce hiring bias, making fairer hiring decisions. Employers including West Midlands Police, Tesco, British Airways and Electricity North West are already using the platform to attract and assess early-career talent. Keighley said: “The UK is rightly focused on how to get more young people earning or learning, but the infrastructure between education and employment is still broken. “CVs don’t work for entry-level talent, job boards don’t reach this generation, and AI has made application volume harder to manage while reducing quality. “We’re rebuilding that system from first principles, combining social distribution, behavioural science and AI to create a fairer, more effective way to connect young people to work. “Our ambition is to become the front door to employment for the next generation.” FUEL Manchester is sponsored by GM Business Growth Hub , S&W and Nybble, with support from Bruntwood SciTech . candidates.evidence_text: Greater Manchester leading UK centre for applied and responsible AI, report finds - Invest Manchester Skip to main content Skip to footer Opens in a new tab Digital, cyber & AI Greater Manchester leading UK centre for applied and responsible AI, report finds Published on October 22, 2026 News First comprehensive baseline study of its kind identifies 663 AI-active firms across Greater Manchester, with more than half founded in the city region Health and life sciences is identified as Greater Manchester’s clearest AI specialism, supported by one of the UK’s most concentrated clusters of AI health research Greater Manchester has the largest AI workforce of any UK region outside London, with an estimated 10,890 people working in AI-related roles across all sectors The study suggests Greater Manchester’s AI ecosystem could grow to around 1,420 firms and support more than 28,000 AI-related jobs by 2035 Greater Manchester is a leading UK centre for the applied and responsible use of AI across key growth sectors, a new report shows . The smart adoption of AI is already making a real difference in health and life sciences, with the future potential to lead to better diagnosis and treatment for patients, in agenda-setting research by the region’s world-class universities, and in powering local economic growth among a community of Greater Manchester businesses developing AI products for customers around the world. Commissioned by the Greater Manchester Combined Authority (GMCA) and produced by Perspective Economics, the Greater Manchester AI Ecosystem Study provides the first comprehensive baseline of AI activity across the city region. The study maps Greater Manchester’s AI businesses, workforce, economic contribution, investment, research assets and growth potential. The findings will inform future decisions on targeted investment and support, enable decision makers to track progress over time, and help to identify the strengths, opportunities and challenges that will shape inclusive and responsible AI growth. The research shows that the city region’s strengths lie in applied AI, using the potentially transformative technology to address challenges within different industries and in improving public services. This strength is underpinned by expertise in higher education and industry to turn research into practical products and solutions. It identifies 663 businesses actively developing or deploying AI across Greater Manchester. More than half (54%) were founded in the city region, rising to 68% among businesses whose primary product or service is AI. The wider AI workforce is estimated at almost 11,000 people, the largest of any UK region outside London. The study also highlights significant future potential. Under a medium-growth scenario, Greater Manchester’s AI ecosystem could expand to around 1,420 businesses by 2035, contributing £1.6bn in annual gross value added (GVA) and supporting a wider AI workforce of more than 28,000 people. Mayor of Greater Manchester Bev Craig said: “As artificial intelligence becomes one of the defining technologies of our time, Greater Manchester is well placed to harness its benefits for our people, businesses and communities. “Our ambition is clear: to be a world-leading AI city region. Not simply a place where AI is developed, but a place where it is applied responsibly and in ways that create lasting public value. “This report provides the most comprehensive picture yet of our AI ecosystem, helping us understand where our strengths lie, where the opportunities are, and how we can build on them in the years ahead. “AI can help us deliver more effective public services, improve health outcomes and accelerate innovation, but growth alone is not enough. We must ensure that innovation creates and protects good jobs, and is developed in a way that is ethical and trusted.” Health and life sciences specialism More businesses whose main product relies on AI are working in health and life sciences than in any other area examined by the study. The city region has a concentration of businesses applying AI in areas including diagnostics, clinical imaging, drug discovery, mental health, patient engagement, and healthcare training. evidence_packet.evidence_text: Iconic Scottish rockers Texas are hitting the road to celebrate 30 years of their seminal record White on Blonde Released in February 1997, Texas’ landmark fourth LP, which is certified 6x platinum in the UK, embraced the band’s love of soul, trip-hop and more Following its immediate, huge success (a Number One album chart placing upon its release, plus five Top 10 singles), the band followed it up with curveball moves including a Wu-Tang Clan collaboration on Say What You Want (All Day, Every Day) that earned them a further Top 10 As part of their upcoming tour, the Glasgow group will play Manchester’s Co-op Live on Fri 29 Oct 2027. Along with a special reissue of the record, Texas have unveiled a brand-new single Another Way To Cry , which you can listen to below “It didn’t feel risky because no one at our label gave a shit,” Spiteri recalls of the attitude towards the band in the UK ahead of White On Blonde . “We were in Glasgow, we made the album in my house and I did all the vocals in the coat cupboard. We had nothing to lose, and anyw Texas will be joined by special guests Del Amitri on all UK and Ireland dates. Pre-sale begins Wed 28 Oct at 10am, with general sale on Fri 30 Oct, also at 10am
