Four-legged family members can also join the fun with the return of Bark Hütte, a pup-sized hütte wi Alongside karaoke, the pop-up’s popular wreath-making workshops will return. Priced at £55 per person, including a glass of fizz or mulled wine, classes will be running on Sun 29 Nov (2pm-4pm) and Tue 1 Dec (6.30pm) Perfect for families, Bae Huttë’s Santa Claus Club is back, too. Enjoy an hour of karaoke with a free hot chocolate per child (up to six children) and colouring pads for the kids. Plus, there’ll be an opportunity to grab a selfie with Father Christmas himself on Sun 13 Dec and Su Booking is strongly advised, but walk-ins are also welcome. There will also be plenty of outdoor seating available under a heated stretched tent, giving Christmas partygoers the chance to get merry without getting cold

candidates.evidence_text: A moonlit community run which aims to empower women and girls to stay active and enjoy outdoor exercise through the winter months comes to Platt Fields Park this week Organised by Manchester Parks in partnership with the running community, the welcoming and inclusive event is not just for experienced runners but for people just getting started and who are looking to become more active, helping them connect with local walking or running groups The event offers a chance to meet local run clubs, find new running partners and pick up tips to run safely through the darker months. Taking place on Thu 22 Oct from 6pm-9pm, the event is open to all genders and abilities, but organisers hope that it will be particularly helpful The first event earlier this year saw 210 people take part to complete a 3k run or walk around the park in a series of waves. Some of the more experienced runners even completed all seven waves and bagged themselves a half marathon The format will be similar this month, with guided runs led by local clubs with several running/jogging waves of a 3k route around the park. Free head torches will be available on a first-come, first-served basis. Attendees are also encouraged to wear lights and fluorescent cloth A small event village will have stalls with representatives from fitness groups, community safety organisations, and charities, and there will be food and drink vendors and music

From years spent languishing in post-industrial decline to being crowned one of ‘the coolest neighbourhoods in the world’ in the blink of an eye. What’s the story here? Find out with Jonathan Schofield Tours, with whom you’ll track Ancoats’ changes by strolling its streets, crossing its canals, and taking a look inside one of its most fascinating buildings Starting at Cutting Room Square, your expert tour guide will reveal the layers of history that make Ancoats special, from its place in establishing Manchester’s reputation as ‘Cottonopolis’ to the notorious street gangs, or ‘scuttlers’, who once patrolled and fought here But this winsome stroll is also about the urban regeneration and cultural energy of Ancoats today, which boasts everything from grassroots theatres to Manchester’s only Michelin-starred restaurant

This guided walking tour will bring those stories to life. Led by a local expert, the experience is set to be a lively introduction to the people, places and ideas that have shaped one of the UK’s most influential cities The tour will begin at Manchester Central Library, that impossible to miss, grand circular landmark on St Peter’s Square. The neoclassical design has made it one of the city’s most-loved buildings, holding thousands of stories in its walls and on its shelves. The square itself ha From here, the tour takes you through the city’s heart, down the colourful streets of the Gay Village and the calming Sackville Gardens. It is here that you will see the monuments that honour Manchester’s role in the fight for equality and the city’s pioneering LGBTQ+ community a This guided tour is filled with monuments and tales from many moons ago. The Medieval Quarter is the perfect place to soak in all that history. It is here where you will see the oldest public library in the English-speaking world, Chetham’s Library . Housed in a beautiful sandsto During all this walking, your guide will point out local street art, hidden corners and stories you’d easily miss on your own. Tales of suffragettes, reformers, musicians and everyday Mancunians who’ve all left their mark on the city in their own way

candidates.lead: Bolton Car Boot Sale at Bolton Car Boot Sale
candidates.evidence_text: Bolton Car Boot Sale is one of the North West's biggest weekly boot sales, held in the hardstanding car park of the Macron Stadium (formerly Reebok), Burnden Way, Horwich, Bolton BL6 6JW. It runs every Sunday from February right through to December, drawing over 300 sellers and thousands of bargain hunters each week. Sellers can arrive and set up from 6:00 AM, with buyers welcomed in from 7:00 AM. Entry costs just £1 per car for buyers. Pitches for sellers are £14 for a car, £20 for a van and £3 for a trailer, with regular and corner pitches available on request. Bring exact change to keep the queue moving, and call organiser Andrew on 07470784644 for more details. Expect hundreds of stalls across the concrete hardstanding pitches, so it goes ahead in most weather. On-site you'll find a 5-star catering service, doughnuts and coffee, ice cream and desserts, a meat auction, fresh fruit and veg, plants, and retro sweet stalls. The sale is dog-friendly, has male and female toilets, ample parking, and kids' rides and bouncy castles to keep little ones entertained.
